notice: RN bank batch 139: Maternity case studies: hyperemesis, PPROM with chorioamnionitis, HELLP syndrome and prenatal screening. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. Also carries the bank-wide catalog (catalog.py): the RN Question Bank and every curated test set.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that distinguish hyperemesis gravidarum from usual morning sickness.

rationale.correct: Weight loss over 5%, ketosis, dehydration and electrolyte loss define hyperemesis.

perOption.r5: A risk factor, not a distinguishing finding.

references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: For each finding, indicate its cause.

rationale.correct: Vomiting causes alkalosis, ketosis and dehydration.

perOption.r5:c1: Gastric and renal losses with alkalosis.
perOption.r5:c2: Gastric and renal losses with alkalosis.
perOption.r5:c3: Gastric and renal losses with alkalosis.

references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: Before giving dextrose-containing fluids, the nurse should give {{b1}} to prevent {{b2}}.

rationale.correct: Thiamine before dextrose.

perOption.b2:a: Glucose without thiamine can trigger it.

references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which parts of the plan should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Daily weight and intake and output
Potassium chloride IV push to correct the level quickly
Large fatty meals to regain weight quickly

rationale.correct: Fluids with potassium, antiemetics, gradual refeeding and monitoring.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Orders
exhibits.body: Thiamine 100 mg IV, then LR with KCl 20 mEq/L at 150 mL/hr. Ondansetron IV.

questions.stem: The client cries and says, "I can't do this for 30 more weeks. Maybe I should end the pregnancy." Which responses are therapeutic? Select all that apply.

options.text: "I can arrange a talk about your options."
"You'll feel terrible later if you do that to your babies."
"It's just morning sickness; everyone has it in the first trimester."

rationale.correct: Validate, offer realistic hope and respect choices.
references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Take action with emotional support in hyperemesis.

exhibits.title: Day 2
exhibits.body: Vomiting twice a day. Ketones trace.

questions.stem: On day 4, for each finding, indicate whether it shows improvement or needs follow-up.

rows.text: New QT prolongation on ECG after several ondansetron doses

rationale.correct: Improvement; QT prolongation needs review.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Highlight the day 3 findings that suggest chorioamnionitis.

rationale.correct: Fever with fetal tachycardia, uterine tenderness and foul fluid after PPROM is chorioamnionitis.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: For each finding, indicate whether it confirms rupture of membranes.

rows.text: Pooling of fluid in the vagina on sterile speculum exam
Urine leak with coughing and acidic pH

rationale.correct: Pooling, nitrazine and ferning confirm rupture.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: Because of chorioamnionitis, the plan is {{b1}}, and tocolytics are {{b2}}.

options.text: antibiotics and keep the pregnancy to 37 weeks

rationale.correct: Antibiotics and birth; no tocolysis.

perOption.b2:a: Keeps the infected fetus in utero.

references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which orders should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Notify the neonatal team for the birth

rationale.correct: Antibiotics, birth, antipyretic and neonatal team.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Orders
exhibits.body: Ampicillin 2 g IV every 6 hours. Gentamicin. Oxytocin induction.

questions.stem: Which actions help coordinate care around the birth? Select all that apply.

options.text: Give the neonatal team the maternal temperature, antibiotic times and gestational age
Arrange a NICU tour or meeting with the neonatologist for the family
Promise the parents the baby will not need the NICU
Omit the fever from the handoff to avoid worrying the team

rationale.correct: Share key data and prepare the family.

perOption.c: Newborn sepsis evaluation depends on it.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Take action to coordinate perinatal care.

questions.stem: After birth, for each finding, indicate whether it shows improvement or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Newborn on IV antibiotics in the NICU, stable
Maternal temperature 39 C on day 2 with tender uterus
Newborn with new grunting and poor feeding

rationale.correct: Improvement; persistent fever or newborn signs need follow-up.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings of HELLP syndrome.

rationale.correct: Hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and low platelets.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: For each complication, indicate whether HELLP syndrome raises the risk.

rationale.correct: HELLP is a severe form of preeclampsia with serious complications.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The definitive treatment is {{b1}}, and {{b2}} is given to prevent seizures.

rationale.correct: Birth with magnesium.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)

Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which parts of the plan should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Labetalol or hydralazine for severe blood pressure
Platelets ready if a cesarean is needed with very low counts
Delay birth for 2 weeks to give steroids more time

rationale.correct: Magnesium, BP control, steroids if possible and blood products.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Orders
exhibits.body: Magnesium 4 g load, then 2 g/hr. Labetalol IV. Plan birth within 24 to 48 hours.

questions.stem: Six hours later, the client has sudden severe right shoulder pain and becomes pale. Review the findings. Which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Call the rapid response or obstetric emergency team
Prepare for emergency surgery and massive transfusion
Give an opioid and reassess in an hour
Massage the abdomen to locate the pain

rationale.correct: Shoulder pain with shock in HELLP suggests liver capsule rupture.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: On postpartum day 2, for each finding, indicate whether it shows recovery or needs follow-up.

rationale.correct: Labs recovering; blood pressure and output need follow-up.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Day 2
exhibits.body: Laparotomy repaired a liver hematoma; cesarean birth. Magnesium continued 24 hours.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that need follow-up.

rationale.correct: An elevated AFP with prior NTD needs a detailed ultrasound.

perOption.r1: Possible open neural tube or abdominal wall defect.
perOption.r4: Needs Rho(D) if amniocentesis is done.

references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize cues of abnormal prenatal screening.

questions.stem: For each test, indicate whether it is a screening or a diagnostic test.

rows.text: Amniocentesis with karyotype and amniotic AFP

rationale.correct: Screening finds risk; diagnostic tests confirm.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The next step is {{b1}}, and AFP can also be falsely high with {{b2}}.

options.text: wrong dates or a multiple pregnancy

rationale.correct: Ultrasound next; dating and twins can raise AFP.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: The ultrasound shows a small lumbar spina bifida. The client is offered amniocentesis. Which actions are part of a sound plan? Select all that apply.

options.text: Refer for genetic counseling before the test
Explain the procedure risk of miscarriage is small
Give Rho(D) immune globulin after the procedure
Respect the client's choice whatever the decision
Tell the client which choice the nurse would make
Schedule the test without consent because it is routine

rationale.correct: Counseling, accurate risk, Rh prophylaxis and respect.
references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

exhibits.title: Ultrasound
exhibits.body: Open lumbar spina bifida; head and heart normal.

questions.stem: After amniocentesis, which instructions should the nurse give? Select all that apply.

options.text: Report fluid leaking, bleeding or cramping
Rest for the remainder of the day and avoid heavy lifting
Expect mild cramping that settles within hours
Ignore decreased fetal movement for a week

rationale.correct: Report leaking, bleeding, fever and reduced movement.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: At follow-up, for each statement, indicate whether it shows understanding or needs more teaching.

rows.text: "I'll plan birth at a center with neurosurgery."
"Next time I'll start 4 mg of folic acid at least a month before trying."
"No amount of alcohol is known to be safe, so I've stopped."
"The one glass of wine caused the spina bifida."

rationale.correct: Planning and prevention; guilt needs gentle correction.

perOption.r2:c1: High-dose folic acid for prior NTD.
perOption.r2:c2: High-dose folic acid for prior NTD.

references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
